analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: וַיֹּאמֶר אַבְרָם means “Abram said” and identifies Abram as the speaker of לִי לֹא נָתַתָּה זָרַע (“you have given me no offspring”).
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix. It serves as the subject of וַיֹּאמֶר (“he said”).
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 68358:2, 66574:0, 66326:3.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected presentative particle without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: look, see (a fact put before the hearer)

analysis.evidence: In לִי לֹא נָתַתָּה זָרַע, “you have not given me offspring,” לֹא negates the perfect verb נָתַתָּה. Abram states what has happened to him.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew negative particle without a prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Abram tells God, לִי לֹא נָתַתָּה זָרַע, “you have given me no offspring.” לִי identifies Abram as the recipient, and זָרַע means “offspring” here because Abram goes on to say that a member of his household will inherit from him.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, second person masculine singular. The ending ־תָּה marks the addressee.

analysis.evidence: Abram says, “You have given me no offspring,” then names a member of his household as his heir. The prospect of that inheritance explains why Abram speaks of his lack of a child.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun. The first vowel lengthens in pause, giving זָרַע.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 67597:18, 67595:5, 67084:4, 65823:6.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to the presentative particle הִנֵּה.
analysis.sense: and there was (what one sees or finds)

analysis.evidence: Abram says that he has been given no offspring (לֹא נָתַתָּה זָרַע), yet a בֶן בֵּיתִי will inherit from him. The construct phrase identifies the heir by his membership in Abram’s household.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state, governed in sense by the following בֵּיתִי (“my household”).

analysis.evidence: Abram says he has been given no offspring. In בֶן בֵּיתִי יוֹרֵשׁ אֹתִי, a member of his household is the subject, and אֹתִי identifies Abram as the person whose estate he will inherit.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute, used as the predicate of בֶן בֵּיתִי.
